scope.notes: 207 rows. Covers Exalted: The Autochthonians' Chapter Two character-creation overview (Attributes/Abilities/Advantages/Virtues/Finishing Touches, plus the bonus-point and experience-cost tables), the universal Alchemical Anima Effect (the five-tier 1-3/4-7/8-10/11-15/16+ Anima Banner table and the Attribute-boost anima power available to every caste), the Alchemical Physiology section (Artificial Metabolism/feeding, Life and Death/dissolution, and Refitting/Essence Advancement/city-metamorphosis), all five Castes (Orichalcum, Moonsilver, Jade, Starmetal, Soulsteel) with their Caste Attributes/Anima Effects/Associations/Sobriquets/Concepts, the apocryphal sixth 'Adamant' Caste sidebar, the full Clarity Trait (the Limit analog: gaining, losing, the 0-10 effects table, and Storytelling guidance) plus its corrupted mirror Dissonance/Gremlin Syndrome, and the new/altered Backgrounds (Class, Vats, Artifact, Backing, Familiar, Manse) including the Building Vats in Creation sidebar and the Followers/Influence/Resources exclusion note. All of Chapter Three (pp. 87-141/PDF 88-142) is inventoried: the Charm-system framing, the two General Charms, and all nine Charm trees (Close Combat, Ranged Combat, Might and Mobility, Social, Stealth and Disguise, Sensory and Spiritual, Medical, Cognitive, Essence and Weaving). The full Alchemical weaving-protocol catalog from Chapter Four (49 rows, printed pp. 142-159/PDF 143-160) is inventoried: the framing/overview rows, the six elemental Golem/automaton protocols, and every other named Man-Machine and God-Machine weaving protocol explicitly cross-referenced in-book from the Man-Machine Weaving Engine and God-Machine Weaving Engine Charms. The rest of Chapter Four's Miracles of the Machine God material that is character-creation-relevant (printed pp. 161, 180-195/PDF 162, 181-196) is also inventoried (31 rows): the three Autochthonian-only alchemical formulae (Sweet Sleep Surrogate Syrup, Friction Banishing Preparation, The Maker's Inertial Bile), the Machines in the Machine God Efficiency/Inspiration sidebar, and the full Autochthonian Technology, Warfare, and Transportation sections (Artificial Textiles, Filter Mask, Photo-Resonant Gel, Arc Protector, Autolabe, Essence Capacitor, Flaw Scanner, Light Amplification Visor, Light Sphere, Omnimodal Wardrobe Unit, Portable Nutriment Recycling Engine, Respirator Module, Courier Drone, Soulgem, Industrial Exoskeleton, Crossbows, Fiber-Weave Bodysuit, Gyroscopic Chakram, Thousand Wounds Gear Style, Beam Klave, Pneumatic Trams, Mechanical Rickshaw, Skimmercraft, and Aerial Skiff). Chapter Four's purely Storyteller-side/NPC material (Autochthonian Thaumaturges' Summoning/Warding/Exorcism/Enchantment/Geomancy subsections, the Eight Divinities and The Core, Custodians/Drones/Design Weavers/Destroyers/Gremlins and their stat blocks, Autochthonian Elementals, Spirit Charms, the Alternative Machine Virtues sidebar, and The Secret of Soulsteel lore sidebar) was reviewed and intentionally excluded as GM/setting/creature content with no character-creation relevance, the same way this book's earlier chapters' pure lore was scoped out. Chapters Five through Seven (The Locust War, The Quest for the Great Source, Engines of Extinction; printed pp. 196-297/PDF 197-298) have now also been reviewed as a scan/triage pass: they are adventure-seed/campaign chapters, and essentially all of their content (war history and timelines, Storyteller/NPC stat blocks including named Alchemical, Deathlord, and mortal characters and their personal artifacts, creature templates like Alchemical/glass beasts, Alchemical Manse adventure-site descriptions, Deathlord-side mortal/nemissary body-augmentation technology and necrotechnology, and general Storytelling/GM advice) was intentionally excluded as out of scope for the same reasons pure lore and NPC-only material has been excluded elsewhere in this book. Exactly one genuinely player-facing, character-creation-relevant item was found and added: the Steamcar, Refurbished, a stat-blocked Autochthonian expedition vehicle from Chapter Six with Charm ports for installed Alchemicals, of the same kind as Chapter Four's Mechanical Rickshaw/Skimmercraft/Aerial Skiff. No further Alchemical-specific Merits/Flaws were found anywhere in Chapters Five through Seven, confirming Gremlin Syndrome/Dissonance remains the only one in the whole book. With this pass complete, all seven chapters of Exalted: The Autochthonians have now been reviewed for character-creation-relevant Alchemical material.

sources.role: Primary Alchemical rules, Charms, Backgrounds, and Autochthonia setting material

rulesNotes: This PDF has a real, clean, selectable text layer (it is not image-based). Text was extracted directly with PyMuPDF (fitz) and cross-checked against the on-page header, which prints the same page number as the 0-indexed PyMuPDF page across every chapter sampled (idx 2 through idx 300): printed page number = 0-indexed PDF page = (1-indexed physical PDF page) - 1. Equivalently, pdfPage (1-indexed, as recorded on every citation below) = printedPage + 1, with no additional front-matter shift anywhere in the book.

Because the text layer is clean, extracted text counts as having been read for every row below. In addition, the tables and several Caste pages that are most vulnerable to multi-column extraction order problems (the Class dot table, the Familiar dot table, the Vats dot table, the Building Vats sidebar, the Clarity effects table, the Alchemical Anima Banners table, and the Orichalcum/Starmetal/Soulsteel Caste pages) were also rendered to page images and visually compared against the extracted text; the extraction matched the rendered pages exactly everywhere it was spot-checked.

The family in this repository's data model is named `alchemical`, but the source book's real title is 'Exalted: The Autochthonians' (not 'The Alchemicals'). bookId/bookLabel use the real title, matching the correction already applied once before in this project.

Alchemicals do not have a Limit Trait. The book's own name for the signature trait mechanic is Clarity (a corrupted, actively malicious mirror version exists too, called Dissonance, gained only via the Gremlin Syndrome Flaw). See the clarity-* and gremlin-syndrome-dissonance rows.

The book still calls Alchemical Exalted's innate magic 'Charms' (it does not rename them), but every Charm is a surgically implanted artifact occupying a General or Dedicated Charm Slot rather than being learned outright the way other Exalted's Charms are. Chapter Three (pp. 87-141/PDF 88-142) organizes Charms into named per-Attribute-cluster trees (General Charms, then Close Combat, Ranged Combat, Might and Mobility, Social, Stealth and Disguise, Sensory and Spiritual, Medical, Cognitive, and Essence and Weaving) rather than by Ability the way Solar/Abyssal Charms are; every tree's own tree diagram was visually cross-checked against the extracted text everywhere it was sampled and matched exactly, including one extraction-order-vs-layout mismatch caught by that check (the small standalone 'Medical Charms I' tree diagram on p. 131/PDF 132 contains only two nodes, Sustained Augmentation of Stamina and Sustenance Replication Engine, even though the surrounding extracted text runs several more Charms together before that diagram appears on the page; those additional Charms actually belong to the larger 'Medical Charms II' diagram on p. 133/PDF 134). All of Chapter Three is now inventoried.

The Man-Machine Weaving Engine and God-Machine Weaving Engine are ordinary Chapter Three Charms (Essence and Weaving Charms sub-tree, the chapter's final section, p. 141/PDF 142) that merely let an installed Alchemical initiate a 'protocol' of Alchemical weaving she has separately learned; the full weaving-protocol catalog itself (the actual list of Man-Machine and God-Machine protocols and their effects, pp. 142-159/PDF 143-160) is now fully inventoried as its own 49 rows, cross-referenced back to the two Weaving Engine Charms.

Checked for additional Alchemical-only Merits/Flaws beyond Gremlin Syndrome by full-text-searching 'merit'/'flaw' across Chapter Two's edges (PDF 56-90), all of Chapter Three (PDF 87-142), the weaving-protocol catalog (PDF 143-160), and the rest of Chapter Four reviewed in this pass (PDF 161-196); no further Alchemical-specific Merit or Flaw exists in any of these ranges. Gremlin Syndrome/Dissonance remains the only one found in the book.

The remainder of Chapter Four (printed pp. 159-195/PDF 160-196, following the weaving-protocol catalog) was reviewed page-by-page via the same clean text layer, with visual spot-checks rendered for every page cited by a row added in this pass (printed 161, 180-195/PDF 162, 181-196) to confirm table/sidebar layout and numeric values. Roughly the first third of that range (Autochthonian Thaumaturges' non-Alchemy subsections, the Eight Divinities/Core, Custodians, Drones, Design Weavers, Destroyers, Gremlins, Autochthonian Elementals, Spirit Charms, and the Alternative Machine Virtues sidebar, printed pp. 159-179/PDF 160-180) is exclusively Storyteller-side lore, NPC stat blocks, and setting flavor with no character-creation-relevant mechanic for Alchemical player characters, and was deliberately not inventoried, the same way this project has scoped out pure-lore chapters elsewhere. The remaining two-thirds (the three Autochthonian-only alchemical formulae, plus the full Autochthonian Technology/Warfare/Transportation sections, printed pp. 161, 180-195/PDF 162, 181-196) is genuinely character-facing artifact and equipment content and is now fully inventoried as 31 rows.

Chapters Five through Seven (The Locust War, The Quest for the Great Source, Engines of Extinction; printed pp. 196-297/PDF 197-298) were reviewed as a scan/triage pass rather than a line-by-line transcription pass, consistent with their nature as adventure-seed/campaign chapters rather than further character-creation rules chapters. The full text of all three chapters was extracted via the same clean PyMuPDF text layer and scanned for anything mechanically player-facing: dot-rated stat blocks, Charm-format 'Cost:'/'Duration:'/'Type:' text, Merit/Flaw point costs, and artifact/vehicle rating tables. A systematic full-text search for 'Merit' and 'Flaw' across all three chapters found no new Alchemical-specific Merit or Flaw (confirming Gremlin Syndrome/Dissonance remains the only one in the book); every dot-rated ('•') line across all three chapters was individually reviewed. The chapters are overwhelmingly adventure plot/timeline narrative (the Locust War's invasion history, the Great Source expedition's plot, the Great Contagion/First and Forsaken Lion's invasion of Autochthonia), Storyteller/NPC stat blocks (named Alchemical Storyteller characters such as Fair-Spoken Rishi, The Guileless Purgator, Lissome Avid Engineer, Many-Pillared Armipotent Colossus, and Miraculous Icon of the Talents and their personal bound artifacts like the Singular Impetus Generation Sledge and the reaver daiklave Vanquisher; mortal NPCs like Yoraka and Stalwart Oak; and the Deathlord First and Forsaken Lion's full Attributes/Virtues/Abilities/Backgrounds/Arcanoi/Charms/Spells stat block), creature templates presented purely as Storyteller-built antagonists (Alchemical beasts and glass beasts, both explicitly built from 'black-box' animal statistics plus a GM-assigned Charm loadout, with no Willpower and treated as automatons), Alchemical Manse adventure-site descriptions (the Jade/Moonsilver/Orichalcum/Soulsteel/Starmetal Manse sections describe one-off recalibration puzroom encounters at Locks of Yugash, not the pre-existing Manse Background), and — in Chapter Seven specifically — mortal thaumaturgical body-augmentation implants (Targeting Lens, Magical Materials Detector, Darksight Eye Plating, Stunpalm) and the Deathlord's soulsteel Necrotechnology implants (Hungry Beacon, Vital Pump, Pyre-Flame Exhaler, Fly-Eye Arrays, Exsanguinating Tongue) built for the Lion's nemissary war bodies, none of which are Alchemical Exalted mechanics. All of this was reviewed and intentionally excluded as adventure plot, GM advice, or NPC/antagonist-only content, the same way this project scopes out pure lore and Storyteller-side material elsewhere in this book.

Exactly one item across all three chapters cleared the bar for a genuinely player-facing, character-creation-relevant mechanic: the Steamcar, Refurbished (printed p. 238/PDF 239, Chapter Six), a fully stat-blocked Autochthonian expedition vehicle (soak, health levels, speed, maintenance/repair rules, and explicit Charm ports for the Electroneural Control Spurs and Universal Pilot Key Charms) given to the player expedition itself rather than bound to a one-off NPC, of the same concrete equipment-stat-block kind as Chapter Four's Mechanical Rickshaw, Skimmercraft, and Aerial Skiff. It was visually spot-checked against the rendered page image before being added as the steamcar-refurbished row. With this pass complete, all seven chapters of Exalted: The Autochthonians (the entire book) have now been reviewed for Alchemical character-creation-relevant material.
